lead.claim: Exercise helps reduce kinesiophobia and improve function after TKA.
lead.context: This systematic review examined if exercise-based rehabilitation could reduce kinesiophobia and improve knee function after total knee arthroplasty.

supporting.claim: Prone positioning and HFOV are not first-line treatments for early PARDS.
supporting.context: This randomized controlled trial investigated whether prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improved ventilator-free days in paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome.

supporting.claim: Hybrid technology is a feasible option for upper limb neurorehabilitation in stroke.
supporting.context: This scoping review explored the use of hybrid technology in upper limb neurorehabilitation for adult stroke patients in hospital settings.

supporting.claim: Psychosocial interventions for ABI need three key components.
supporting.context: This realist evaluation aimed to identify essential program theories for psychosocial interventions in young adults with acquired brain injury.

supporting.claim: Could timing stroke rehab closer to sleep improve motor recovery?
supporting.context: This review explored the hypothesis that scheduling motor therapy close to sleep could enhance motor memory consolidation and recovery after stroke.
